mainTopic: Whether gifts like חלה, the מתנות and תרומה may be brought to a כהן on יום טוב, which תנא the משנה follows, and whether husking and crushing produce is permitted on יום טוב.
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ברייתא that gives lashes for cooking and for kindling (הבערה) on יום טוב. רבי יוחנן rejects it as unreliable. He adds that even if it is authentic, it follows בית שמאי, who do not accept the rule of מתוך. בית הלל accept מתוך, so for them kindling on יום טוב carries no lashes. A new משנה follows: בית שמאי forbid bringing חלה and the priestly מתנות to a כהן on יום טוב, and בית הלל permit it. The גמרא asks whose version of this argument the משנה follows. It brings three versions, from רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and אחרים, and concludes that the משנה can fit רבי יהודה or אחרים, who differ only about טפלה. The הלכה follows רבי יוסי, so even תרומה may be brought to a כהן, as the story of רב טובי's wine shows. Finally, רבא permits husking kernels and crushing legumes on יום טוב. אביי challenges him twice; the first challenge is answered, and the answer to the second begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: lashes for הבערה
steps.stepSummary: These are the closing words of the ברייתא, listing the last of the five lashes: הבערה.
steps.simpleTranslation: …because of kindling.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the ברייתא at its very last words. The final reason listed for lashes is lighting a fire (הבערה) on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא (which began on the previous lines) counts five sets of lashes for cooking the גיד הנשה in milk on יום טוב and eating it. Two of those reasons are יום טוב melachot: cooking on יום טוב (the first item) and kindling on יום טוב (the last item). These two are the target of what רבי יוחנן says next.

keyTerms.meaning: Kindling, lighting a fire (one of the 39 מלאכות)

phrases.english: because of kindling.
phrases.notes: The fifth and final set of lashes in the ברייתא, which began on the previous amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם הַבְעָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא recited by the תנא before רבי יוחנן (begun on the previous amud).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who cooks the גיד הנשה in milk on יום טוב and eats it also receives lashes for kindling a fire on יום טוב.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן dismisses the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells the תנא to take this teaching outside, because counting הבערה and בישול is not a reliable teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go out and teach it outside. Kindling and cooking are not a real teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן rejects the part of the ברייתא that gives lashes for kindling and cooking on יום טוב. He calls it unfit for the בית המדרש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking and kindling are permitted on יום טוב for food purposes. So רבי יוחנן holds they should not carry lashes at all. He does not try to explain the ברייתא; he simply says it is not an authentic teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Go out and teach it outside, meaning this teaching does not belong in the study hall
It is not a real teaching, not authentic

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'מִשְׁנָה' does not mean a line from our printed משנה. It means 'an authentic, reliable teaching.' רבי יוחנן is saying the ברייתא is not trustworthy.

phrases.english: He [Rabbi Yochanan] said to him: Go out and teach it outside,
kindling and cooking is not a [genuine] teaching.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: פּוֹק תְּנִי לְבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the last two items of the ברייתא just recited.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the lashes for הבערה and בישול on יום טוב, not the other three lashes.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Kindling and cooking are permitted on יום טוב, so they cannot carry lashes. The teaching is therefore not authentic.

steps.title: Even if authentic, it follows בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: Even if the ברייתא is authentic, it follows בית שמאי. They do not accept the rule that 'since it was permitted for a need, it is permitted even without a need.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want to say it is a real teaching, it is בית שמאי. They say: we do not say that since carrying out was permitted for a need, it is also permitted without a need. Here too, we do not say that since kindling was permitted for a need, it is also permitted without a need.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a fallback answer. If the ברייתא is genuine, it follows the minority view of בית שמאי, not the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי hold that carrying on יום טוב is permitted only when it serves a food need. Carrying without such a need stays forbidden. The same logic applies to kindling: kindling that does not serve food stays forbidden, and here the cooking was for forbidden food, so for בית שמאי there are lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want to say, i.e., even if we grant this
Since it was permitted for a need
Carrying from one domain to another
Not for a need, without a food purpose

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of מתוך is a key tool in all the laws of יום טוב. Here we see that it can decide whether a whole category of מלאכה carries lashes on יום טוב.

phrases.english: And if you want to say it is a [genuine] teaching —
it is [the view of] Beit Shammai, who say:

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמְרִינַן מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁהוּתְּרָה הוֹצָאָה לְצוֹרֶךְ
phrases.english: we do not say that since carrying out was permitted for a need
it was also permitted not for a need.
Here too, we do not say:
since kindling was permitted for a need,
it was also permitted not for a need.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר מִשְׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, fallback way to deal with the ברייתא, in case the first rejection is not accepted.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution to a minority opinion (בית שמאי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא might seem to be a standard ruling that kindling on יום טוב carries lashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: It reflects only בית שמאי's view, because they reject מתוך. It is not the accepted הלכה.

steps.title: Why it cannot be בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows why the ברייתא cannot follow בית הלל: they accept מתוך, so kindling would be fully permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if it were בית הלל: since they say that once carrying out was permitted for a need it is also permitted without a need, here too, once kindling was permitted for a need, it is also permitted without a need.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the attribution to בית שמאי. It shows that according to בית הלל there could be no lashes for kindling on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל apply the מתוך logic to carrying. The same logic must apply to kindling. Once kindling is permitted for food, the Torah's prohibition of kindling on יום טוב is lifted entirely, so no lashes are possible.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of הלל, whose rulings are usually the הלכה

steps.whatToRemember: According to בית הלל, the rule of מתוך means that kindling and cooking on יום טוב are not punished with lashes even without a food need. A ברייתא that gives such lashes is either not authentic or follows בית שמאי.

phrases.english: For if it were Beit Hillel —

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאָמְרִי מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁהוּתְּרָה הוֹצָאָה לְצוֹרֶךְ
phrases.english: since they say that since carrying out was permitted for a need
it was also permitted not for a need,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁהוּתְּרָה הַבְעָרָה לְצוֹרֶךְ —
phrases.english: here too: since kindling was permitted for a need —
it was also permitted not for a need.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי בֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 3 by ruling out the other possible author (בית הלל).
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא must be attributed to בית שמאי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בית הלל's known position of מתוך regarding הוצאה, applied by analogy to הבערה.

steps.title: New משנה: bringing חלה and מתנות to a כהן on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי forbid bringing חלה and the priestly מתנות to a כהן on יום טוב, whether they were separated before יום טוב or on יום טוב. בית הלל permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: בית שמאי say: we do not bring חלה and the priestly gifts to the כהן on יום טוב, whether they were separated yesterday or today. And בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a fresh מחלוקת. The question is whether one may carry חלה and the priestly gifts to a כהן on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי forbid it in both cases: when the gifts were separated before יום טוב and when they were separated on יום טוב. בית הלל permit it. This connects to the topic we just saw, since בית הלל accept מתוך for carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of dough given to a כהן
The priestly gifts from an animal: the foreleg, the jaw, and the maw
Since yesterday, i.e., before יום טוב

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה opens the next sugya. The גמרא will ask which תנא's version of this argument the משנה follows: רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי, or אחרים.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: Beit Shammai say:
one may not bring challah and [priestly] gifts
to the kohen on Yom Tov,
whether they were separated since yesterday,
or whether they were separated today.
And Beit Hillel permit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The topic shifts, but the theme of carrying on יום טוב continues.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי forbid bringing חלה and מתנות to a כהן on יום טוב in all cases. בית הלל permit it.

steps.title: בית שמאי compare the gifts to תרומה
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי argue that חלה and מתנות are gifts to the כהן just like תרומה. Since תרומה may not be brought on יום טוב, the other gifts may not be brought either.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: We learn this from a comparison. חלה and the other gifts are a gift to the כהן, and תרומה is a gift to the כהן. Just as we do not bring תרומה, so too we do not bring the gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the משנה, בית שמאי give the reason for their rule: all the כהן's gifts belong to one family, so they follow the same law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides already agree that תרומה is not brought to the כהן on יום טוב. בית שמאי use that agreed point as an anchor. Since חלה and מתנות are also 'a gift to the כהן,' they say the same ban should apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, an argument from likeness: two things share a label, so they share a law
The portion of produce given to a כהן
A gift belonging to the כהן
We bring or carry (to the כהן)

steps.confusionAlert: Here גזירה שוה does not mean the formal method of learning from two matching words in the תורה. It just means 'these are alike, so they share one law.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה:
phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to them: an analogy:
Challa and the gifts are a gift to the priest,
and teruma is a gift to the priest.
Just as one may not bring teruma,
phrases.notes: Both sides agree on this point.

phrases.english: so too one may not bring the gifts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives בית שמאי's reason for the ruling stated in step 5
steps.raayaObject: בית שמאי's ban on bringing חלה and מתנות on יום טוב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The agreed-upon ban on bringing תרומה on יום טוב

steps.title: בית הלל reject the comparison
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל answer that תרומה is different, because it may not be separated on יום טוב. These gifts may be separated on יום טוב, so they may also be brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to them: No. You may say this about תרומה, which one is not allowed to separate on יום טוב. Can you say it about the gifts, which one is allowed to separate?
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל break בית שמאי's comparison by pointing out a real difference between תרומה and the other gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why can't תרומה be brought? Because it is the kind of thing that cannot be separated on יום טוב. חלה and the animal gifts are allowed to be separated on יום טוב. So the reason behind the ban on תרומה does not carry over to them.

keyTerms.meaning: If you said (this about one case): the opening of a rebuttal
Separating (a gift from produce or an animal)

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי: all the כהן's gifts are alike, so none may be brought. בית הלל: what counts is whether the gift may be separated on יום טוב.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to them: No,
if you said this about teruma,
which one is not permitted to separate,
will you say it about the gifts,
which one is permitted to separate?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל: לֹא, אִם אֲמַרְתֶּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made in step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between תרומה and the other gifts
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: תרומה is banned because it may not be separated on יום טוב, and that reason does not apply to the gifts

steps.title: Whose opinion does the משנה follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא first assumes the משנה means 'separated today' = from an animal slaughtered today, and 'separated yesterday' = from an animal slaughtered yesterday. Then it asks which תנא holds this.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: You might think 'separated today' means slaughtered today, and 'separated last evening' means slaughtered last evening. Whose opinion is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by setting up a working reading of the משנה. It then asks which תנא fits that reading, preparing the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, בית שמאי forbid bringing even gifts from an animal slaughtered on יום טוב itself. That is a strict position, so the גמרא wants to know who taught the dispute this way.

keyTerms.meaning: It enters your mind (a first assumption that may change later)

steps.confusionAlert: 'קא סלקא דעתך' means this is only a first assumption. The גמרא may later read the משנה differently.

phrases.english: GEMARA
It enters your mind
that 'separated today' means slaughtered today,
and 'separated last evening' means slaughtered last evening.
Whose opinion is our mishna?

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's discussion of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds the משנה's version of the dispute, read according to the assumed meaning

steps.title: Not רבי יוסי or רבי יהודה, but אחרים
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the משנה follows neither רבי יוסי nor רבי יהודה. It follows the תנא called אחרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Not רבי יוסי and not רבי יהודה, but אחרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by naming the תנא our משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are several versions of what בית שמאי and בית הלל argued about. Only the version of אחרים matches the משנה as read in step 8. Next, the גמרא will bring רבי יהודה's version to show how it is different.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others': the name used for a certain תנא, identified as רבי מאיר

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Not Rabbi Yosei and not Rabbi Yehuda,
but Acherim.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אֶלָּא אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows אחרים, not רבי יוסי or רבי יהודה

steps.title: רבי יהודה's narrower version of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says both sides agree that gifts separated before יום טוב may be brought together with gifts from today. They argue only about bringing the earlier gifts by themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי יהודה said: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about gifts separated before יום טוב. Everyone agrees one may bring them together with gifts separated and slaughtered today. They argued only about bringing them by themselves: בית שמאי say one may not bring them, and בית הלל say one may.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא of רבי יהודה to show that his version of the argument does not match our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהודה's version, בית שמאי agree that today's gifts may be brought, and yesterday's gifts too when they go along with today's. The only argument is over yesterday's gifts brought alone. Our משנה (as read in step 8) has בית שמאי forbidding both kinds, so it cannot follow רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how one argument can be reported in different versions. Finding the matching version tells us which תנא a משנה follows.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not argue

phrases.aramaic: עַל הַמַּתָּנוֹת שֶׁהוּרְמוּ מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב
phrases.english: about gifts separated on the eve of the Festival
that one may bring them along with the gifts
separated today and slaughtered today.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא לְהוֹלִיכָן בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן,
phrases.english: They argued only about bringing them by themselves,
for Beit Shammai say: one may not bring them,
and Beit Hillel say: one may bring them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source showing that רבי יהודה's version differs from our משנה
steps.raayaObject: That our משנה does not follow רבי יהודה

steps.title: בית שמאי's reasoning in רבי יהודה's version
steps.stepSummary: In רבי יהודה's ברייתא, בית שמאי use the same comparison to תרומה to forbid bringing the earlier gifts by themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is how בית שמאי would reason: חלה and the gifts are a gift to the כהן, and תרומה is a gift to the כהן. Just as one may not bring תרומה, so too one may not bring the gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and gives בית שמאי's reason. It uses the same words as the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording is the same as step 6, but here it supports a narrower ruling. In רבי יהודה's version, the ban covers only gifts separated before יום טוב and brought alone.

phrases.english: And this is how Beit Shammai would reason:
Challa and the gifts are a gift to the priest,
and teruma is a gift to the priest.
Just as one may not bring teruma,
so too one may not bring the gifts.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכָךְ הָיוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי דָּנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יהודה's ברייתא with בית שמאי's reasoning
steps.raayaObject: בית שמאי's ban on bringing earlier-separated gifts by themselves
steps.raayaSupportSource: The comparison to the ban on bringing תרומה

steps.title: בית הלל's reply in רבי יהודה's version
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל give the same answer as in the משנה: תרומה may not be separated on יום טוב, but these gifts may be, so they may also be brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to them: No. You may say this about תרומה, which one is not allowed to separate. Can you say it about the gifts, which one is allowed to separate?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with בית הלל rejecting בית שמאי's comparison, using the same words as the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning matches step 7. Since these gifts are the kind that may be separated on יום טוב, even ones separated earlier may be brought alone. The difference between רבי יהודה's version and our משנה is only in which gifts the argument is about, not in the reasoning.
steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה (as first read) has בית שמאי forbidding even today's gifts, which matches אחרים. רבי יהודה limits the argument to gifts separated before יום טוב and brought alone. Both versions use the same תרומה comparison and the same reply.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to them: No,
if you said this about teruma,
which one is not permitted to separate,
will you say it about the gifts,
which one is permitted to separate?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל: לֹא, אִם אֲמַרְתֶּם בִּתְרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects בית שמאי's comparison within רבי יהודה's ברייתא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison of the gifts to תרומה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ban on תרומה comes from the ban on separating it, which does not apply to these gifts

steps.title: רבי יוסי's version of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that the gifts may be brought on יום טוב. They argue only about תרומה: בית שמאי forbid bringing it, and בית הלל allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about the gifts; everyone agrees they may be brought. They argued only about תרומה. בית שמאי say: we may not bring it. בית הלל say: we may bring it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives a second version of the argument, this time in the name of רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהודה's version (Steps 10-12), the gifts were the subject of the argument. רבי יוסי moves the argument to a different item. For him, bringing the gifts is permitted by everyone, and the real debate is over תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who gives a different version of the argument
We may bring / carry (to the כהן)
The priestly portion taken from produce

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the versions. For רבי יהודה, the argument is about bringing the gifts. For רבי יוסי, everyone permits the gifts, and the argument is about תרומה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not argue
about the gifts, that we may bring them;
they argued only about terumah,
for Beit Shammai say: we may not bring it,
and Beit Hillel say: we may bring it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל עַל הַמַּתָּנוֹת שֶׁמּוֹלִיכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing version of the same ברייתא argument that רבי יהודה reported
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, all agree the gifts may be brought on יום טוב. The argument is only about תרומה.

steps.title: בית הלל compare תרומה to the other gifts
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל argue that חלה, the gifts, and תרומה are all gifts to the כהן. Since the gifts may be brought, תרומה may be brought too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is how בית הלל reasoned: חלה and the gifts are a gift to the כהן, and תרומה is a gift to the כהן. Just as we may bring the gifts, so we may bring תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל give their reason for allowing תרומה to be brought on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a comparison argument. All of these items belong to the same group: gifts for the כהן. Since everyone agrees the gifts may be brought, בית הלל say תרומה should be treated the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of dough given to a כהן

phrases.english: And this is how Beit Hillel would reason:
challah and the gifts are a gift to the kohen,
and terumah is a gift to the kohen;
just as we may bring the gifts,
so we may bring the terumah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכָךְ הָיוּ בֵּית הִלֵּל דָּנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives בית הלל's reason inside רבי יוסי's version
steps.raayaObject: That תרומה may be brought to a כהן on יום טוב
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to the gifts, which everyone agrees may be brought

steps.title: בית שמאי reject the comparison
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי answer that the gifts may be separated on יום טוב, but תרומה may not. So the comparison fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: No! You may say this about the gifts, which one is allowed to separate on יום טוב. Will you say it about תרומה, which one is not allowed to separate?
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי push back against בית הלל's comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי point to a real difference between the two items. Separating the gifts is allowed on יום טוב, but separating תרומה is not. Since תרומה cannot even be separated on יום טוב, it should not be brought either. Notice that this is the same separation difference used in Step 12, but here it is used for the opposite side.

keyTerms.meaning: No! If you said (this about one case)

phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to them:
No! If you said this about the gifts,
which one is allowed to separate on Yom Tov,
will you say it about terumah,
which one is not allowed to separate?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי: לֹא, אִם אֲמַרְתֶּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects בית הלל's comparison in Step 14
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the gifts and תרומה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The gifts may be separated on יום טוב, but תרומה may not, so the two are not alike

steps.title: The version of אחרים
steps.stepSummary: אחרים say everyone agrees that תרומה may not be brought on יום טוב. The argument is only about the gifts: בית שמאי forbid bringing them, and בית הלל allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחרים say: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about תרומה; everyone agrees it may not be brought. They argued only about the gifts. בית שמאי say: we may not bring them. בית הלל say: we may bring them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a third version of the argument, from the תנא called אחרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחרים take the opposite position from רבי יוסי. For them, תרומה is forbidden by everyone, and the argument is about the gifts. That makes their version look like the משנה, which also places the argument on the gifts.

keyTerms.meaning: "Others": the title of an unnamed תנא

steps.whatToRemember: There are three versions. רבי יהודה: the argument is about bringing earlier gifts by themselves. רבי יוסי: everyone permits the gifts, and the argument is about תרומה. אחרים: everyone forbids תרומה, and the argument is about the gifts.

phrases.english: Others say:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not argue
about terumah, that we may not bring it;
they argued only about the gifts,
for Beit Shammai say we may not bring them,
and Beit Hillel say we may bring them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל עַל הַתְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the third version of the argument, which Step 9 said the משנה follows
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to אחרים, all agree תרומה may not be brought. The argument is only about the gifts.

steps.title: Does the משנה follow only אחרים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה matches אחרים and not רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say the משנה follows אחרים and not רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: After quoting all three versions, the גמרא suggests a conclusion: the משנה fits only אחרים. This sets up רבא's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This suggestion still rests on the reading from Step 8, that the gifts came from an animal slaughtered today. On that reading, the משנה cannot fit רבי יהודה, who says everyone permits gifts that are separated today.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion that may be rejected)

phrases.english: Shall we say it follows Acherim
and not Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא אֲחֵרִים הִיא וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the three versions just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the משנה limited to the view of אחרים?

steps.title: רבא: separated today, but slaughtered yesterday
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that the משנה only says the gifts were separated today. The animal itself could have been slaughtered yesterday.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Does the משנה say "separated today and slaughtered today"? It only says "separated." Really, the animal was slaughtered last night.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects the assumption from Step 8 by reading the words of the משנה more carefully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 assumed that "separated today" means the animal was slaughtered today. רבא notes that the משנה mentions only separating. So the animal could have been slaughtered before יום טוב, with the gifts separated on יום טוב. That opens the way for the משנה to fit רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / in truth (here is the true reading)

steps.confusionAlert: Separating the gifts and slaughtering the animal are two different actions. They can happen on different days.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Does it teach "that were separated today
and that were slaughtered today"?
It teaches only "that were separated,"
and really, their slaughter was last night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִי קָתָנֵי שֶׁהוּרְמוּ מֵהַיּוֹם וְשֶׁנִּשְׁחֲטוּ מֵהַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undoes the assumption behind Step 17's suggestion
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading from Step 8 that "separated today" means "slaughtered today"
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה speaks only of separating, not slaughtering
steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the sugya now works with the case where the animal was slaughtered before יום טוב and the gifts were separated on יום טוב.

steps.title: Then the משנה follows רבי יהודה, not אחרים?
steps.stepSummary: If the animal was slaughtered yesterday, perhaps the משנה fits רבי יהודה and not אחרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then shall we say it follows רבי יהודה and not אחרים!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא suggests the reverse: maybe the משנה fits only רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's argument concerned gifts from before יום טוב. רבא's new reading also has an animal slaughtered before יום טוב. So it now seems that the משנה matches רבי יהודה and may not fit אחרים.

phrases.english: Shall we say it follows Rabbi Yehuda
and not Acherim!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא וְלֹא אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from רבא's new reading
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim from Step 9 that the משנה follows אחרים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the animal was slaughtered yesterday, the case matches רבי יהודה's version, so perhaps not אחרים's

steps.title: אחרים can also refer to animals slaughtered yesterday
steps.stepSummary: The משנה can still fit אחרים. Their argument can also be about animals slaughtered before יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say it follows אחרים, they too are speaking about animals that were slaughtered last night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה does not have to be limited to רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing forces us to read אחרים as speaking about an animal slaughtered on יום טוב. Their argument about the gifts can also be about animals slaughtered before יום טוב. So the משנה can fit אחרים as well.

phrases.english: Even if you say it follows Acherim,
they are speaking about those slaughtered last night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case behind a תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אחרים are speaking about an animal slaughtered on יום טוב, so the משנה cannot be theirs
steps.terutzMaskana: אחרים can also be speaking about an animal slaughtered before יום טוב

steps.title: Then אחרים would be the same as רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: If אחרים also speak about animals slaughtered yesterday, how is their view any different from רבי יהודה's?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, that is the same as רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in Step 20: it seems to erase the difference between the two תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both תנאים would be arguing about the same case: gifts from an animal slaughtered before יום טוב. If so, why does the ברייתא list them as two separate views?

phrases.english: If so,
that is the same as Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי הַיְינוּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 20
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that אחרים also speak about animals slaughtered yesterday
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two separate views in the ברייתא must differ somewhere, but now they seem identical

steps.title: The difference: secondary gifts brought along
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה and אחרים differ about טפלה: earlier gifts brought along together with today's gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is the case of secondary gifts brought along with others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by naming the one case where the two תנאים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said both sides agree that earlier gifts may be brought together with today's gifts (Step 10). For אחרים, the argument covers even that case: בית שמאי forbid it, and בית הלל allow it. So the two versions still differ.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
Secondary: earlier gifts brought along with today's gifts

steps.whatToRemember: Bottom line: the משנה can follow either רבי יהודה or אחרים, once we read it as gifts separated today from an animal slaughtered yesterday. The two תנאים differ only about טפלה. רבי יהודה says everyone permits it, while for אחרים, בית שמאי forbid it.

phrases.english: The difference between them is the secondary (brought-along) gifts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ טְפֵלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21 by naming the practical difference
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to a practical difference (נפקא מינה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה and אחרים say exactly the same thing
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ about טפלה. רבי יהודה says all permit it, while for אחרים it is part of the argument, and בית שמאי forbid it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה fits both רבי יהודה and אחרים. The two differ only about טפלה.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי in the dispute about bringing gifts to a כהן on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: After all the back-and-forth about the views of רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי, and אחרים, the גמרא now gives the final practical ruling: we follow רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that בית הלל permit bringing priestly gifts to a כהן on יום טוב. Since the הלכה follows בית הלל, the practical result is that one may bring תרומה and similar gifts to a כהן on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose version of the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל is accepted here

steps.whatToRemember: Practical bottom line: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, so even תרומה (not only חלה and the מתנות) may be brought to a כהן on יום טוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the long discussion of the dispute with a clear ruling that can be applied in real life, as the next story shows.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha is like Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל הלכה כרבי יוסי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the three-way dispute among רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and אחרים quoted in steps 10-16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The halacha follows רבי יוסי: everyone permits bringing the מתנות, and בית הלל (whom we follow) permit bringing even תרומה to a כהן on יום טוב.

steps.title: רב טובי asks about bringing תרומה wine to a כהן
steps.stepSummary: רב טובי has a jug of תרומה wine and asks רב יוסף whether he may bring it to a כהן on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב טובי, son of רב נחמיה, had a jug of תרומה wine. He came before רב יוסף and asked: May I bring it to a כהן today, on יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story in which the ruling we just learned becomes a real-life question. This sets up רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly the case in the dispute: carrying a priestly gift to a כהן on יום טוב. The question is whether that is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן
Now, today (here meaning on יום טוב)

phrases.english: Rav Tovi, son of Rav Nechemya,
had a jug of teruma wine.
He came before Rav Yosef.
He said to him: What is the law about bringing it
to a kohen now, on the festival?

steps.triggerLanguage: מהו לאמטויי לכהן האידנא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a practical case to which the ruling of step 23 applies.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is it permitted to bring תרומה wine to a כהן on יום טוב?

steps.title: רב יוסף answers with שמואל's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers by quoting רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, so the wine may be brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question by quoting the ruling from step 23. That means yes, he may bring the wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא really does repeat the ruling here, but now it is used to decide an actual case. Following רבי יוסי means בית הלל permit bringing the gift, so רב טובי may bring the wine to the כהן on יום טוב.
steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף does not openly say 'yes.' His answer is the quote itself. Because the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, the answer is that it is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rav Yehuda said
in the name of Shmuel: The halacha is like Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה הכי אמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל הלכה כרבי יוסי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24 using the ruling of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is permitted, because the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, under whose version בית הלל allow it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, תרומה may be brought to a כהן on יום טוב.

steps.title: The host asks about crushing mustard stalks on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The host of רבא בר רב חנן asks whether he may crush mustard stalks and eat the seeds on יום טוב. רבא בר רב חנן does not know, so he goes to ask רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The host of רבא בר רב חנן had bundles of mustard stalks. He asked him: May one crush them and eat from them on יום טוב? רבא בר רב חנן did not have an answer, so he came before רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: whether one may crush or husk produce on יום טוב. This step sets up the question that רבא will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mustard seeds are still inside their stalks. Getting them out means crushing, which looks like the forbidden work of threshing. The question is whether this is allowed on יום טוב for food needed that day.

keyTerms.meaning: To crush or rub out seeds
He did not have an answer

phrases.english: The host of Rava bar Rav Chanan
had bundles of mustard stalks.
He said to him: What is the law about crushing them
and eating from them on the festival?
He did not have an answer at hand,
so he came before Rava.

steps.triggerLanguage: מהו לפרוכי ומיכל מנייהו ביום טוב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to bringing gifts to a כהן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May one crush mustard stalks to get the seeds and eat them on יום טוב?

steps.title: רבא permits husking and crushing on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers with a teaching: on יום טוב one may husk kernels by rubbing them, and one may crush legumes. So the mustard may be crushed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: One may husk kernels and crush legumes on the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the host's question by quoting a general rule that permits rubbing kernels and crushing legumes on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crushing mustard stalks is like crushing legumes, so it falls under the same permission. רבא treats this kind of food preparation as allowed on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Rubbing kernels between the fingers to remove the husks

phrases.english: He said to him: One may husk kernels
and crush legumes on the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוללין מלילות ומפרכין קטניות ביום טוב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is permitted: husking kernels and crushing legumes are allowed on יום טוב, so crushing mustard is allowed too.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may husk kernels and crush legumes on יום טוב.

steps.title: אביי cites a ברייתא about husking before שבת
steps.stepSummary: אביי begins his challenge with a ברייתא. Kernels husked on ערב שבת may be winnowed on שבת only by hand, not with a basket or a large bowl.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: One who husked kernels on ערב שבת may, the next day, blow off the chaff from hand to hand and eat. But not with a basket, and not with a large bowl.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts to challenge רבא by quoting a ברייתא. This first part is about שבת and sets up the comparison with יום טוב that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Notice the case: the husking was done before שבת, on ערב שבת. On שבת itself, only a very unusual way of winnowing is allowed: blowing between the hands. Using any vessel is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him from a תנאי source
A basket sometimes used for sorting

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
One who husks kernels on Shabbat eve,
the next day may blow off the chaff from hand to hand, and eat.
But not with a basket, and not with a large bowl.

steps.triggerLanguage: איתיביה אביי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge to רבא's ruling in step 27 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that one may husk kernels on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא describes husking done before the holy day, which hints that husking on the holy day itself is not allowed. The point becomes clear in the יום טוב clause.

steps.title: The ברייתא's rule for husking before יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: kernels husked on ערב יום טוב may be winnowed little by little on יום טוב, even with a basket or a bowl, but not with real winnowing tools.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who husked kernels on ערב יום טוב may, the next day, blow off the chaff a little at a time and eat, even with a basket or a large bowl. But not with a board, not with a winnowing tool, and not with a sieve.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the rule for יום טוב, which is more lenient than שבת. This still sets up אביי's precise point, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב, food preparation is more lenient, so even a basket or a bowl may be used. Tools made especially for winnowing are still forbidden, because they are used for large amounts and look like ordinary weekday work. But again, the husking itself happened on ערב יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A board or tablet used in processing grain

phrases.english: One who husks kernels on festival eve,

phrases.aramaic: לְמָחָר מְנַפֵּחַ עַל יָד עַל יָד, וְאוֹכֵל
phrases.english: the next day may blow off the chaff a little at a time, and eat,
even with a basket and even with a large bowl.
But not with a board,
and not with a winnowing tool, and not with a sieve.

steps.triggerLanguage: המולל מלילות מערב יום טוב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא that אביי began in step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's permission to husk kernels on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even the lenient יום טוב case talks only about husking done on ערב יום טוב, which suggests husking on יום טוב itself is forbidden.

steps.title: אביי's inference: only before יום טוב, not on it
steps.stepSummary: אביי draws the point: the ברייתא allows husking only on ערב יום טוב, which implies it is forbidden on יום טוב itself. That contradicts רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ערב יום טוב, yes; on יום טוב itself, no!
steps.whatsHappening: Here אביי makes the punch of his challenge: the ברייתא's wording implies that husking on יום טוב itself is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If husking on יום טוב were allowed, the ברייתא would not need to say the husking was done on ערב יום טוב. Its choice of case shows that only winnowing is allowed on יום טוב, not the husking itself. That clashes with רבא, who permits husking and crushing on יום טוב.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never openly says 'husking on יום טוב is forbidden.' אביי infers it from the fact that the ברייתא specifically speaks about husking done on ערב יום טוב.

phrases.english: On festival eve, yes;
on the festival itself, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: מערב יום טוב אין ביום טוב לא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenging inference from the ברייתא quoted in steps 28-29.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement that one may husk kernels and crush legumes on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows husking only on ערב יום טוב, which implies it is forbidden on יום טוב, directly against רבא's ruling.

steps.title: The ברייתא's wording just copies the first clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers אביי. Husking may really be allowed on יום טוב itself. The ברייתא only said 'from ערב יום טוב' to match its first clause, which said 'from ערב שבת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say husking is allowed on יום טוב itself, the ברייתא still makes sense. Since the first part said 'from ערב שבת', the second part also said 'from ערב יום טוב'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. It explains that the words 'from ערב יום טוב' in the ברייתא do not prove that husking is forbidden on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי read the words 'from ערב יום טוב' as a deliberate limit. The גמרא says the wording is only there for style: the ברייתא echoed the first clause, where 'from ערב שבת' really was necessary because husking is forbidden on שבת. So nothing can be inferred about יום טוב, and רבא's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say: introduces a way the opposing view can still hold
Since / because of: the wording was used only to match something else
The first clause of a teaching
The latter clause of a teaching

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying the ברייתא's words are meaningless. 'From ערב שבת' in the first clause is fully meaningful. Only the matching phrase in the second clause is explained as copied wording.

phrases.english: Even if you say that husking is permitted on the Festival itself,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא can still fit רבא's view.

phrases.english: since it taught in the first clause, 'from Shabbat eve',
phrases.notes: On שבת husking really is forbidden, so this wording was needed there.

phrases.english: it also taught in the latter clause, 'from Festival eve'.
phrases.notes: This is matching wording only, not a real limit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בְּיוֹם טוֹב, וְאַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's inference from step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic parallelism: the wording in the second clause is borrowed from the first clause and carries no inference.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'From ערב יום טוב' implies that husking on יום טוב itself is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase only mirrors 'from ערב שבת', so husking on יום טוב may be allowed, as רבא said.

steps.title: Husking would require separating תרומה on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא again. If husking is allowed on יום טוב, the grain becomes ready food during יום טוב and would need תרומה separated then. But the משנה says one may not separate תרומה on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, we have found a case of תרומה that a person is allowed to separate on יום טוב. But we learned in the משנה: 'No, if you said this about תרומה, which a person is not allowed to separate on יום טוב...'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a new challenge against רבא from a different angle: the laws of תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain still in its husk was not yet ready food, so it did not yet need תרומה. If husking is allowed on יום טוב, the grain becomes ready during יום טוב, and one would have to separate תרומה before eating it. But in our משנה, בית הלל themselves say that תרומה may not be separated on יום טוב, so רבא's ruling seems to lead to an impossible result.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces an unacceptable result of the other side's view
The portion of produce given to a כהן
Allowed to separate it (on יום טוב)
And we learned in a משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge links the question of preparing food on יום טוב to the ban on separating תרומה on יום טוב. That ban is the very reason בית הלל give in the משנה on this daf.

phrases.english: If so, we have found a case of teruma
phrases.notes: Grain husked on יום טוב becomes newly obligated in תרומה.

phrases.english: that one is permitted to separate on the Festival,
phrases.notes: He must separate it before eating, so it would have to be allowed.

phrases.english: but we learned in the mishna: 'No, if you said this about teruma,
phrases.notes: בית הלל's reply to בית שמאי in our משנה (step 7).

phrases.english: which one is not permitted to separate on the Festival, etc.'!
phrases.notes: Both sides agree that תרומה may not be separated on יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן מָצִינוּ תְּרוּמָה שֶׁזַּכַּאי בַּהֲרָמָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered in step 31, אביי opens a second, separate challenge against רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling (step 27) that one may husk kernels on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Husking on יום טוב makes the grain newly obligated in תרומה, which would force separating תרומה on יום טוב. The משנה assumes that separating תרומה on יום טוב is forbidden.

steps.title: The גמרא begins its answer: no difficulty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to defend רבא by saying אביי's challenge is not a real difficulty. The full explanation comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא announces that it has an answer to אביי's תרומה challenge and is preparing to explain it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לא קשיא' tells us the גמרא will resolve the contradiction instead of giving up רבא's ruling. Usually this means it will draw a distinction that removes the conflict. That distinction comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult: opens a resolution of a challenge

phrases.english: This is not difficult,
phrases.notes: The explanation follows on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the answer to אביי's תרומה challenge in step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Opening formula; the actual distinction is given in the following step.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Husking on יום טוב would force a forbidden separation of תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not yet stated; the גמרא only declares that the challenge can be resolved.
